A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from DMDSpeech to DMOSpeech. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-synthesis evaluations, human listening studies, component ablations, diversity analyses, and acoustic-feature results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the human evaluations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: DMDSpeech is renamed DMOSpeech, but the latent diffusion architecture, four-step DMD2 procedure, conditional discriminator, CTC/SV losses, and training strategy remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LibriLight training, CommonVoice/LibriLight auxiliary-model training, and LibriSpeech test-clean evaluation. The appendix continuation task and conditional versus varying-prompt diversity scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the teacher, NaturalSpeech 3, StyleTTS-ZS, DiTTo-TTS, VoiceCraft, CLaM-TTS, and XTTS in their respective comparisons. The expanded YourTTS discussion does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The training configurations, evaluation metrics, 16-kHz evaluation audio, 47- and 80-sample listening comparisons, and 3,711-sample objective evaluation remain unchanged. Appendix E retains the same participant selection and rating-validation procedures.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendices A, B, and D retain the same sampling-step, CTC/SV-loss, batch-size, mode-coverage, acoustic-feature, and human-rating correlation analyses. No additional analysis is reported within v2.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same standard-error reporting, significance thresholds and annotations, and correlation significance reporting. The documented listening-study counts and repeated-synthesis procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: The result entries, numerical values, and plotted findings in Tables 1–7 and Figures 2–5 are unchanged after matching the renamed model. For example, Table 3 still reports WER 1.94, SIM 0.69, and RTF 0.07 for the proposed model.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and derivations in Section 3 and Appendix C, including Equations 1–38, are retained. The new discussion of optimization difficulties adds conceptual arguments rather than formal definitions, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central distillation and direct-metric-optimization contributions remain. However, v2 explicitly claims the first distilled TTS model consistently outperforming its teacher, broadens the introduction to improvements across all metrics, and describes acceleration as orders of magnitude. These strengthen existing claims rather than introduce a new contribution.

C2.justification: The introduction adds explanations involving unstable or prohibitively expensive backpropagation through iterative sampling and uninformative perceptual gradients at high noise levels. The interpretations of mode shrinkage, metric trade-offs, and ethical and diversity limitations were already present in v1 and remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 updates the stated audio-sample website for the DMOSpeech name and adds an access link to a noise-level illustration. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and existing code/data access instructions remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not establish external resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds a specific contrast with YourTTS's earlier speaker-similarity optimization and refines the novelty argument around gradient propagation through all components. It removes background references to Bai et al. (2022), Johnson et al. (2016), Popov et al. (2021), and Yang et al. (2023), while retaining the principal prior-work coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial portions of the introduction, and all three related-work discussions are extensively rewritten around end-to-end metric optimization. The title and model name change throughout, although the methods, experiments, conclusions, and appendix organization largely retain their wording and structure.

P2.justification: The same six figures and eight tables are retained without substantive display changes. Model names in captions and table labels are updated, Preprint running headers are added, and text and references undergo limited page reflow.

improvement.justification: The rewritten opening explains the optimization motivation more directly, but introduces overstatements and unresolved citation markers. The introduction broadly calls metric–human correlations strong although Figure 5 retains weak WER correlations of -0.16; the abstract claims orders-of-magnitude acceleration although Section 4.3 reports 13.7-fold acceleration over the teacher. These changes reduce precision and editorial reliability despite clearer framing. The unchanged methods and empirical evidence limit the overall deterioration.
